about: Entirely fictional acceptance cases (status family M-8 with sub-codes M-8-1 orchard grafting trainee, M-8-2 glassblowing apprentice, M-8-3 trail patrol assistant, M-8-4 tea-leaf processing technician; invented agency 가상 산마루체류청, regions 가상 단풍 관할 / 가상 바위 관할, offices 가상 안개 사무소 / 가상 솔숲 출장소, documents, amounts and the other-family code W-2-5); not law. Authored only from trusted_evidence_spec.md (005-S revision); the 005-R acceptance suite was read for format only (schema, case keys, registry shape, the expected block, mention-group and forbidden-pattern notation). No code, run output, notebook, benchmark or other suite was read, and all patterns were written fresh. Focus, caps on an amount (spec 5, 005-S): permitted-within-a-cap positives, where a correct answer states the cap with a negation and must still be released as a permission, A05S-01, A05S-02, A05S-03, A05S-37, A05S-44, A05S-59, A05S-61, A05S-62, A05S-63 (ko 03/59/61, en 01/37/62, vi 02/44/63; hours, days, a count and money); cap-negatives, where the evidence prohibits the activity and also mentions a number, A05S-38, A05S-39, A05S-45. Kept from 005-R: two-case positives A05S-16, A05S-31, A05S-32, A05S-40, A05S-43, A05S-67; sub-code-exception negatives A05S-70, A05S-71. Ambiguities recorded: (1) The Korean cap forms are listed as endings after a number; a unit and particle in between ('주 15시간을 넘지 않는', '6회를 넘을 수 없다') is read as the same form, as in the spec's own example. (2) The cap-negative evidence attaches the number with forms the spec does not list as caps ('주 10시간 이하의 짧은 일도 같다', '30일이 지난 뒤에도 같다', '500,000원 이하인 경우에도 같다'), so the evidence stays a prohibition; an answer that recasts the number as a cap ('넘지 않으면 할 수 있다', 'as long as sales do not exceed …') is a permission once the cap is removed and therefore a polarity reversal, so the affirmative patterns do not count cap negations as negation. (3, superseded) The spec gives no Vietnamese form without được/thể ('không quá N'); the patterns treat it like a cap, and no expected value depends on it. (4) The polarity patterns are lexical and sentence-scoped: a ban pattern skips any sentence that carries a number (digits inside status codes or evidence ids do not count), a number word, or a cap or condition word, so a ban sentence that also repeats the number can escape it; each cap and cap-negative case was tested with correct answers (no fire) and outright-ban or allowed answers (fire) in its language. (5) Whether hours or a count are values for the value check is not stated; every cap value is in the cited admissible text, so no expectation depends on it. (6) Mention groups assume the 005-R normalisation (lower case, whitespace removed); comma and dot thousand separators are listed as extra spellings. Implementer note after review: ambiguity (3) is resolved, spec 5 lists bare 'không quá N'; spec 5 (005-S) was also widened before freezing so that natural cap wordings the review found (up to four words between the negation and the cap word, English number words, 'above', 'in excess of', 넘게/넘겨/보다 많이, nhiều hơn, trên) are caps; no expected value changed.
